newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-KNAUSS WINS SUPER-G, HEADS OVERALL STANDINGS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KNAUSS WINS SUPER-G, HEADS OVERALL STANDINGS.

text.p: Austrian Hans Knauss won the first men's super-G of the World Cup season on Monday to leap to the top of the overall standings.
Knauss, who won a super-G at Valloire last season, was timed at one minute 23.26 seconds as he finished ahead of compatriot Guenther Mader with Swiss Steve Locher in third place.
Knauss, whose second, third and fourth places in giant slaloms this season had put him third overall before Monday's race, now has 297 points, pushing Norwegian Kjetil Andre Aamodt into second.

The Austrian team enjoyed a near clean sweep of the top places in both races at Val d'Isere after taking the first four in Sunday's downhill. Patrick Ortlieb, third in the downhill, was fourth in the super-G.
The super-G was put back to Monday after bad weather on Saturday forced the postponement of the downhill for 24 hours.
The men's World Cup circus now crosses the border into Italy for a slalom at Madonna di Campiglio on Tuesday when Italian Alberto Tomba is expected to make his debut of the season.
At the end of the week, there will be two downhills in Val Gardena and a giant slalom in Alta Badia.
